scope: Backend-only Android view availability/default/visibility preferences, persistence, legacy migration and local change events; no Android logical tree or GPUI controls installed.
adaptations: IntelliJ project/IDE services and Studio flag overrides are explicit Rust inputs.
JVM System properties and options-directory lookup are supplied launcher-resolved configuration; clearing updates that configuration object.
Application settings XML becomes a narrow standalone JSON preference backend with fallible load/save; the product adapter must persist state before reporting migration durable.
Notification balloons and UsageTracker/protobuf events become typed return values for local caller delivery; no network messages or telemetry.

Legacy Java properties migration retains unrelated configuration bytes/comments/line endings and removes all equivalent escaped/continued property entries. This strengthens preservation over Properties.store without changing any original assertion.
VM-options comparison remains case-sensitive true with last value winning, and all matching custom options are removed. The Rust backend reports removal only when a custom entry was actually removed.
remaining_product_wiring: project_panel Android/filesystem view selector and explicit backend capability input, after Android logical tree exists
Existing settings service adapter: persist the true filesystem-view preference before legacy cleanup; provide retry/recovery or rollback when persistence fails
Run filesystem reads/atomic writes on the background executor; marshal typed results to the foreground without blocking GPUI
Publish local change events and GPUI information notifications only after preference durability; clear the shared launcher-resolved legacy configuration once
Node visibility icon rendering using the backend preference
